card.occupation: Retired toolmaker (worked as a toolmaker and later a general maintenance fitter at small engineering firms around Tipton, Wednesbury and Oldbury; finished full-time work at 63)
card.education_detail: Left secondary modern school at 16 with a couple of CSEs, then did a four-year engineering apprenticeship with day release at the local technical college, where he got a City & Guilds in mechanical engineering craft practice
card.household: Lives with his wife Sandra, 64, in a two-bed ex-council semi they bought in the late eighties. Two grown-up children: a son in Halesowen and a daughter in Telford. Three grandchildren, who visit most Sundays or every other Sunday.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Black Country, father worked at a foundry and mother did shifts in a shop. Church of England by upbringing. He and Sandra go to the local parish church at Christmas, Easter and for christenings and funerals, rather than every week. He would call himself Christian without thinking much about it.
card.professional_persona: Spent most of his working life on lathes and grinders, then moved into maintenance when the toolroom work dried up. He was good with his hands and could fix most things, but never kept the paperwork up. Job sheets were always late and his toolbox was a mess. He didn't want to be a supervisor and turned it down twice. Now he does the odd job for neighbours, and family when they ask.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong West Brom fan. Had a season ticket in his forties but now watches on telly or follows it on the radio. Played Sunday league as a young man. These days the most exercise he gets is walking to the shop or the bookies, because his knees are bad.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. Has the radio on, mostly Free Radio or BBC WM, and likes the old rock and Motown he grew up with. Watches quiz shows and repeats of old detective series. Hasn't been to a theatre since the grandkids' panto three years ago.
card.travel_persona: Same caravan park near Rhyl most summers for over twenty years, plus the odd day out to Weston. Went to Spain once for their silver wedding and didn't like the heat or the food. Doesn't have a passport that's in date and isn't bothered.
card.culinary_persona: Plain food. Sandra does most of the cooking. He likes a fry-up at weekends, faggots and peas, a Sunday roast and a bacon bap from the café by the market. Has been told to cut back on sugar because he's borderline diabetic, and only half does. A pint or two of mild or bitter at the club on a Friday.
hobbies_and_interests: Pottering in the shed, mostly not finishing things
Horse racing on telly, a small bet on Saturdays
The working men's club on Fridays
Tinkering with an old lawnmower engine he's had in bits for two years
Feeding the birds in the back garden
skills: Fixing bikes and mowers for the grandkids and neighbours
card.career_goals: None really. He is retired and happy enough to stay that way. He might do a few cash-in-hand fixing jobs if asked, but isn't looking.
card.voice: Quiet, slow, low-energy, short answers. He often stops after one sentence and waits to see if that's enough. Light Black Country accent, with the 'i' in words like 'like' and 'time' sounding broader. Will occasionally say 'give it me' or call a roll a 'bap', and calls the evening meal 'tea'. Uses 'er' as a filler, plus 'sort of' and the odd 'you know' or 'to be honest'. Says 'yow' for 'you' now and again without noticing. Leaves silences long and doesn't rush to fill them. If he doesn't follow a question he says 'sorry?' or 'how d'you mean?'. Not unfriendly, just not a talker.
card.typing: Slow, two-finger typing. Mostly lowercase, sometimes starts with a capital. Few commas, sometimes no full stop at the end. Usually leaves apostrophes out ('dont', 'its'). Short replies like 'not really', 'yes ok', 'fair health knees are bad'. The odd typo he doesn't go back to fix.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit awkward. Polite but gives the minimum, so he can seem flat or uninterested at first. Doesn't ask questions back. Warms up slightly if the talk turns to football, his old job or the grandkids, but never really gets chatty. Prefers to get it over with.
small_things: The price of a pint at the club
Bin collection getting messed about by the council
The lawnmower engine he still hasn't sorted
Sandra signing him up for this study
deeper_things: Being told he's pre-diabetic and worrying about ending up like his dad, who had a leg off
Feeling a bit lost since he stopped work, with not much to fill the days
Wishing he'd been less stubborn with his son when he was a teenager
The firm he did his apprenticeship at closing down and the area never being the same
Not being much of a churchgoer but praying sometimes when someone's poorly
card.webcam_photo: A laptop camera view angled slightly upwards from a dining table, showing Graham from the chest up, sitting a little too close and slightly off-centre to the left. Daylight comes from a window to his right, so that side of his face is brighter and the other is in mild shadow. He has a round, ruddy face with deep lines around the eyes, grey stubble, and a neutral, slightly wary expression with his mouth closed and his eyes looking just below the camera. Short grey hair, thinning on top. Wire-framed reading glasses pushed up on his forehead. He wears a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed school photo of two grandchildren and a West Brom calendar on a nail. Part of a brown leather settee with a folded crocheted blanket is visible, and a doorway to a hall with coats hanging on hooks. A corner of a glass-fronted cabinet with ornaments sits on the right edge of the frame.
